title: Launch Slate Stakeholder Bandwidth Optimizer
creator: Mariana Soto
description: Design and deliver a scheduling assistant (the Bandwidth Optimizer) that recommends launch windows for feature rollouts across runtime/console/API surfaces by balancing stakeholder bandwidth, engineering capacity, and cross-product risk. This ticket captures the PM scope: requirements, evaluation criteria, rollout plan, and handoffs to the orchestration/infra teams for implementation of the automatic suggestion engine and a manual override UI in Console.
background: We currently coordinate release trains with a mix of Slack threads, spreadsheets, and ad-hoc runbook meetings. This creates friction when multiple teams (runtime, console, API) want overlapping launch windows and when engineering resources or on-call bandwidth are constrained. Recent postmortems (incidents #INC-2026-03 and planning delays for runtime-quantization-rollout) highlighted missed optimizations and avoidable conflicts that would be reduced by a system-aware scheduling assistant.
goal: Provide a lightweight, actionable recommendation for launch windows that: (1) minimizes cross-team overcommitment, (2) respects SLO/capacity constraints for runtime-backed launches, and (3) surfaces alternatives when conflicts exist—reducing manual coordination time by at least 40% for PMs and release owners.
success_metrics: Time-to-schedule measured as median hours from initial launch request to assigned window reduced by 40%
Number of cross-team launch conflicts detected during cutover week reduced by 50%
Adoption: >= 60% of release owners use optimizer suggestions for Q2 launches
Fewer urgent rollbacks attributable to capacity contention (target: -30% YoY for launches using optimizer)
scope_in: Data model for team bandwidth (calendars, on-call rotations, sprint commitments)
Capacity constraints ingest for runtime (throughput lanes, GPU reservations) and console/API (deploy windows, migrations)
Console UI: window suggestions with conflict explanation and manual override
Exportable schedule to cross-team calendar and Slack notification template
scope_out: Fully automated booking of infra capacity (out of scope for MVP)
Advanced ML-based prediction of incident risk (future initiative)
Billing/commit adjustments for Dedicated customers (separate procurement flow)
proposal: Build a lightweight scoring engine that ingests: team-declared bandwidth (weekly available hours), current sprint load (story points), on-call schedule, and runtime capacity forecast. Each launch request is scored against windows across the next 8 weeks. The engine will output top 3 windows with conflict reasons and a confidence score. Expose these suggestions in the Console release planner with buttons: Accept, Propose Alternative, Request Manual Review. A small feature-flagged rollout will allow limited teams to trial the suggestions before full rollout.
rollout_plan: Week 0-2: Requirements & data contract (PM + Infra + Eng + Design)
Week 3-4: Prototype scoring engine and CSV ingest of historical launches for calibration
Week 5-6: Console UI mock + usability session with 6 release owners
Week 7: Internal dogfood (runtime and console product teams only)
Week 8-10: Gradual enablement to 30% of release owners with monitoring
Week 11: Full enablement if adoption and metrics thresholds met
stakeholders: Release Owner Representatives: runtime-team, console-team, api-team
risks: Data freshness: inaccurate sprint or on-call data will produce bad suggestions
Resistance: release owners may distrust automated suggestions without clear explanations
Edge cases: emergency rollouts and security fixes must bypass optimizer cleanly
Integration effort: aligning data contracts across infra and multiple teams may take more time than planned
acceptance_criteria: Scoring engine returns top-3 windows for a submitted launch request with explanation payload
Console displays suggested windows and allows Accept/Propose Alternative/Request Review
Telemetry: events for suggestion_view, suggestion_accept, suggestion_reject are emitted
Pilot cohort (runtime + console) reports scheduling time reduced in a weekly survey
notes: Design must include a lightweight explanation UI (e.g., 'Conflict: runtime GPU pool at 75% for this week')
We should default to conservative capacity estimates for external customer-facing launches
Consider a manual 'hard-block' toggle for security/infra teams to reserve blackout windows
